requirement:
A parse result retains the file identity, bytes, and outline prepared from
those bytes together. Selecting an item from that result uses the retained
snapshot under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.snapshot`.
rationale:
structural: Structural obligations in `requirements.sdk.sources.provider_results.parse_snapshot`: (1) "A parse result retains the file identity, bytes, and outline prepared from those bytes together." An alternative result type that held only the outline, or that re-read the bytes later, would give the same output for a single call but would violate this. (2) "Selecting an item from that result uses the retained snapshot." An alternative that took the outline from the parse result but re-read the text from the provider to slice excerpts would violate it.

Evidence for (1): `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources.rs#fn[parse_snapshot]` is marked impl. It reads the text of the `SourceFile` it was given, so it does not refetch. It builds the outline from that text. It returns `ParsedSource { resource: id.clone(), source, outline }`, which keeps identity, bytes and outline together. The struct `ParsedSource` (fields `resource`, `source`, `outline`) is reached from this marked root through the type it returns, so it needs no marker of its own. `defaults::parse` and `LocalSources::parse_sync` only delegate to `parse_snapshot`, so they are not roots.

Evidence for (2): `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources.rs#mod[defaults]/fn[search_structure_with]` is marked impl. It takes `provider.parse(...)` and reads the text from `parsed.source.text()`. It runs the rule over that text. It selects the innermost node from `parsed.outline` using the same text. It builds the excerpt from the same text, and it rejects a result whose `parsed.resource` differs from the requested id. It never re-reads the resource, so selection uses the retained snapshot.

The remaining clause concerns the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.snapshot`. That requirement is a cited declaration and supplies context only.

behavioral: The subject has two obligations. First, a parse result keeps the file identity, bytes and outline together, and the outline is prepared from those same bytes. Second, selecting an item from that result uses the retained snapshot. The second obligation relies on `requirements.sdk.outlines.snapshot`, so I checked only that the subject's tests apply it to a parse result.

**Identity and bytes**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/tests.rs#fn[defaults_use_provider_primitives_and_keep_one_parse_snapshot]` asserts that `parsed.resource` equals the requested id. It asserts that the parsed text starts with "version 0" and that exactly one read happened during the parse.
- The same test then reads the resource again and gets "version 1". It asserts that the earlier parse result still holds "version 0".
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/tests.rs#fn[local_provider_scopes_paths_and_rejects_resources_outside_its_root]` parses with both `parse_sync` and `parse` and asserts the retained bytes are equal. It rewrites the file to "changed\n". It asserts that a fresh parse sees the new text and that the earlier retained result still holds "hit\n".
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[empty_sources_errors_and_retained_snapshots_remain_distinct]` asserts `parsed.id().path` and an empty selector. After the file is edited, it asserts that `parsed.text()` is still the original two-line text.

**Outline prepared from those bytes**
- The first test calls `parsed.outline.node_lines` with the retained text. It asserts the result contains "version 0" after the underlying file has moved on.
- The second test asserts the retained outline yields exactly "hit" from the retained text after the edit to "changed\n". The new text has a different length, so an outline built from the new bytes would not produce this.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/tests.rs#fn[list_read_only_provider_supports_selected_language_parse_and_structural_search]` asserts that `parsed.outline.resolve("fn[provided]")` succeeds. It also asserts the parsed text equals the provider text. This shows the outline was built from the parsed bytes. It repeats the resolve check for the explicit-language and extension-chosen cases.

**Selecting an item from the retained snapshot**
- Each test selects from the outline of the result, using `node_lines` or `resolve`. The selection is read against the retained text. Later file changes do not affect it.

I found no behavioural obligation without a test and no marking gap. All four tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.
